accuracy.evidence: Every product and quotient in the lesson, lab data and challenge was recomputed (JUMP, TURN, GRID, DIV, CNT, QS and all items). The sign rule matches CCSS 7.NS.2a-c ((-1)(-1) = 1 from the distributive property; quotients of integers with a non-zero divisor follow the same sign rule) and NC 2014 KS3 number. The adult text gives the distributive-law proof, (-1)(-3) + 1(-3) = 0, not only the pattern, and says plainly that the rule is for multiplying and dividing, not adding. Parameterised items keep the divisor non-zero (b, a from 2 to 9) and every division is exact.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented directed-number slips (Hart 1981 CSMS; Vlassis 2004; Gallardo 2002): 'two negatives make a positive' carried over to addition (practice p4, mastery m6, challenge tags addrule), negative x negative given as negative (prediction 2, grid cell 4, tag negneg), a mixed-sign product made positive (jump options, tag mixed), the sign dropped in division (division cards, tag drop) and miscounting three or more negatives (count step, prediction 4, m7, tag count). Distractors also include the add-instead-of-multiply answer (3 + 4 = 7 among the jump cards).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagsignrule is built on this topic's own mechanism: repeated jumps of a negative size drawn as hops, a (-3) times-table pattern continued past zero, a draggable multiplier from -4 to 4 that visibly flips the product arrow across zero, a two-by-two sign grid, division checked by its inverse multiplication, and a negatives-pairing count. It is not the adding/subtracting walker of flagdirnum. Gate: under 30% shingle overlap with every other flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds the rule before it is stated: hops show 3 x (-4) landing at -12, the table forces (-1) x (-3) = 3 to keep adding 3, dragging the multiplier below zero turns the arrow round, and only then does the grid ask for the summary rule. Division is answered by a check multiplication shown under each question; the count step labels each negative so pairing is visible. Each done message confirms in one line.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: (-1) x (-3) = -3 (the pattern step shows 3), (-4) x 2 = 8 (the arrow flips to -8), (-12) / (-3) = -4 (the check multiplication shows 4), and (-1)(-1)(-1) = 1 (pairing leaves one negative over). Each step's done message reveals the locked-in prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Eight challenge questions, each wrong option tagged to its own slip with its own message: negneg, addrule (with the -7 worked), mixed, drop (with the check 3 x 6 = 18), count (odd/even negatives), add (added instead of multiplied) and times (multiplied instead of divided). In-step feedback also names the slip: 'That adds 3 and (-4)', 'right size but on the wrong side of 0', 'The sign is wrong: check (-4) x ...'.

readability.evidence: Learner lesson for ages 11 to 13; kid text uses short sentences and one idea per paragraph (jumps, pattern, short rule, division, many numbers) and is within the learn/readability.py learner limit; adult text within its limit. Canvas headings are one line naming the sum; terms product, quotient and integer appear in the adult text with plain meanings in the kid text.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no filler phrases, under 12% six-word overlap with any other lesson). Each kid paragraph teaches one step (jumps, the pattern past zero, the short rule, division by its check, pairing negatives); the adult paragraphs give the curriculum link, the distributive-law reason, the named mistakes with research, and a lab summary. Lab step text is one sentence each.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark: answer cards are a full-width row of three 60+ px cards, the multiplier slider spans the width with a 15 px radius handle and 52 px hit band, the number line labels every second or third integer so labels never collide at 390 px, the pattern table rows are at least 30 px, and nothing is clipped.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: one per answer card labelled with the whole sum ('3 x (-4) lands on -12'), Next jump, First number - 1 and + 1 for the slider, '+ positive' and '- negative' labelled with the product. say() updates the canvas aria-label and the polite live region after every action, and the slider reports the live product while dragging. The walk gate's axe run is clean (WCAG 2.1 AA) in both themes on desktop and iPhone.
